$comment: SDK PIN — the second half of the analyzer-stability guarantee.
Directory.Build.props sets AnalysisMode=All with TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, so
every analyzer rule the SDK enables is a BUILD ERROR. Without a global.json,
each machine and each CI runner uses whatever SDK it happens to have, and a new
SDK can enable new CA rules with no package release and no commit of ours — the
LINT gate then reds on unchanged source and no local run reproduces it. Pinning
AnalysisLevel to a number fixes the rule SET; pinning the SDK here fixes the
toolchain that supplies the analyzers, the code-style rules and the compiler.
rollForward=latestPatch: this exact feature band (10.0.1xx), newest patch. Patch
releases do not add analyzer rules, so builds keep working on a slightly newer
runner image while a FEATURE-band or major bump stays deliberate. allowPrerelease
is false so a preview SDK installed for something else is never silently used.
The library still multi-targets net8.0/net9.0/net10.0 — TargetFrameworks in the
csproj is what we SHIP for; this is only the SDK that BUILDS it. Bump this and
AnalysisLevel in Directory.Build.props together, with whatever new findings the
new level reports fixed in the same commit.
